tip.title: Space practice over several days
tip.why: A 2006 review pooled over 300 experiments on memory and found that studying the same material in separate sessions, with gaps between them, produced better long-term recall than putting the same total time into one sitting. Cramming feels productive because it helps tomorrow, but the spaced version is what is still there weeks later.
how: Pick one thing you want to remember, such as a new Spanish phrase or a concept from work.
Review it today for five to ten minutes, then again tomorrow, then in three days, then in a week.
Each time, try to recall it from memory first and only then check yourself.
tip.src: Cepeda, Pashler, Vul, Wixted & Rohrer · Psychological Bulletin, 2006
tip.ask: What is one thing I could review again tomorrow instead of finishing it tonight?

markets.headline: Chips bounced on Friday after Thursday's rout, but a hot jobs report and fresh AI-regulation worries left all three major indexes lower for the week.
points: The S&P 500 closed at 7,376.86 (+0.31%) and the Nasdaq Composite at 24,579.42 (+1.09%), while the Dow fell 0.46% to 51,285.73. For the week the S&P 500 lost 2.68%, the Nasdaq 3.37% and the Dow 0.94%, after Thursday's 4.36% drop in the S&P 500 and 5.52% in the Nasdaq, its worst day in about 19 months.

Chipmakers rebounded: AMD jumped about 11%, Marvell about 5.7% and Micron about 5.1%, the Philadelphia chip index gained about 4.2%, and Nvidia rose 2.78% to $186.64 after losing roughly 9% on Thursday. Intel rose 7.71% to $56.28, but Atlassian fell about 16% on a weaker data-center outlook.

October payrolls rose 165,000 against forecasts near 60,000 and unemployment slipped to 4.1%, which raised the odds of a Fed rate hike next month. The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 2 basis points to roughly 4.86%.

Tesla rose 4.23% to $358.22 after falling 10.77% on Thursday, when the Democratic midterm sweep raised questions about AI regulation and the data-center buildout. SpaceX's stock (SPCX) gained about 8.6% to $134.27 after a 9% drop; Musk told investors Tesla would probably rent Optimus robots.

In an Oct. 30 video he laid out two paths for bitcoin, one of which has buyers defending a roughly $73,000 to $77,000 support zone, and he has flagged a break below about $74,900 as a risk. Bitcoin is trading near $76,000 now, inside that zone, after falling 5.6% on Thursday alongside the stock selloff. He has also argued that the fourth quarter could set a new low for the cycle.

brief.lede: Chips bounced on Friday after Thursday's rout, though a hot jobs report kept the week red. Agility's stock debut, Musk's plan to rent Optimus, Anthropic's roadshow and a Nov. 13 Starship target round out the news.

articles.title: Chips bounce after the worst Nasdaq day in 19 months, then a hot jobs report
body: Chip stocks recovered on Friday, but not enough to undo a week of damage. The Nasdaq Composite rose about 1.1% to **24,579.42** and the S&P 500 gained 0.3% to 7,376.86, while the Dow slipped 0.5% to 51,285.73. All three indexes still finished the week lower, with the S&P 500 down 2.7% and the Nasdaq down 3.4%.

The bounce followed Thursday's rout, when the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq 5.5%, its worst session since April 2025. Nvidia dropped roughly 9% that day and lost about **$450 billion** in market value, and CNBC reported that Qualcomm fell by a similar amount after weak guidance. Reports tied the selling to the Democratic midterm sweep, with investors worried about tougher AI regulation and a slower data-center buildout. One estimate cited by a market summary, from UBS, said 30% to 40% of planned US data-center capacity additions through 2028 could face construction delays.

On Friday AMD jumped about 11%, Marvell and Micron rose more than 5%, and the Philadelphia chip index added about 4%. Nvidia recovered 2.8% to $186.64. Not everything bounced: Atlassian fell about 16% on a weaker data-center revenue outlook, and Japan's Nikkei dropped nearly 6%.

The other shock was the labor market. October payrolls rose by **165,000** against forecasts near 60,000, and unemployment edged down to 4.1%. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.86%, and traders now see a better chance of a Fed rate hike at next month's meeting. That matters for AI stocks because higher yields make expensive growth shares harder to justify.

The next test is whether the rebound holds without help from rates. Analysts quoted this week split on whether the move simply priced in the election, or whether more pain is coming for AI infrastructure names as investors reassess demand.

articles.title: Agility becomes the first pure-play humanoid stock, and its orders come with conditions
body: Agility Robotics began trading on Nasdaq as **AGLT** on Thursday after closing its merger with a blank-check company, Churchill Capital Corp XI. It opened at $11.26, dipped below that, and closed at **$11.51**, up 2.2% on the day, on a day when the Nasdaq fell 5.5%. The company said the deal raised about $465 million before expenses and values it near $2.5 billion.

The headline demand number is more than **$300 million** in committed multi-year orders for Digit 5, the next-generation version of its warehouse robot. Agility said those orders depend on contractual milestones and final product specifications. One filing-based report says they are for 1,000 robots from a single customer, paid for as a three-year service, and reports put first Digit 5 deliveries in the first half of 2027.

The financial picture is early-stage. One report citing its financials put 2025 revenue at about $1.8 million and the net loss at $138.1 million. A public listing now means those numbers will be scrutinized every quarter, in a market where humanoid economics are still unproven. Semafor quoted its chief executive calling it a challenging market but saying Agility is well capitalized.

What it means: this is the first real public-market price for a humanoid maker that already has robots working commercially. China's Unitree listed in Shanghai in August, but Agility is the first US pure play. How the stock trades over the coming weeks will signal whether investors will pay for humanoid revenue before it is large, or only after.

articles.title: Musk says Tesla will probably rent Optimus, as Tesla and SpaceX shares swing
body: Speaking in a fireside chat with Ron Baron at Baron Capital's annual conference on Friday, Elon Musk said Tesla will **probably rent** Optimus robots rather than sell them. Tesla still plans to start delivering to outside companies around the end of 2027, so those first deliveries now look like rentals. In a follow-up post on X, Musk wrote that Optimus would eventually be available to rent or buy, so renting looks like the starting model rather than a permanent rule.

Coverage of the talk put the build cost near **$30,000** per robot, falling toward $20,000 over time, and quoted Musk saying Optimus will be about five times as productive as an average person. Tesla gave no rental price or contract terms, so the economics remain open. Renting would let Tesla keep control of the robots and bill for output, but it also means carrying the hardware on its own books.

The talk landed in a rough week for Musk's stocks. Tesla fell 10.8% on Thursday to $343.69 as the Democratic midterm sweep raised questions about AI regulation, the data-center buildout and a possible SpaceX merger, then rose 4.2% on Friday to $358.22. SpaceX's stock fell about 9% on Thursday to $123.62 and recovered about 8.6% to $134.27 on Friday. Reports say Tesla's board formed a special committee in October to look at a closer relationship with SpaceX, though I found no direct comment from Musk on a merger at the conference.

For anyone tracking Optimus, the useful change is the business model. A rental fleet makes reliability and uptime the product, which is a harder test than a one-time sale, and the first real numbers should come with the late-2027 deliveries.

articles.title: Anthropic's roadshow is expected next week, with no price range yet
body: Anthropic has still not published a price range for its planned Nasdaq listing under the ticker **ANT**. Its Nov. 2 amended filing left the offering price blank, and one outlet that checked EDGAR on Friday found no newer filing. Bloomberg and The Information, as relayed by other outlets, reported that the investor roadshow would begin the week of Nov. 9, and Reuters pointed to a mid-November debut, though no date is official.

Valuation talk has moved down with the market. Reports citing Bloomberg put discussions at **$1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion**, possibly as low as $1.1 trillion, after the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.4% on Thursday. The Financial Times had earlier cited a target of $1.25 trillion to $1.75 trillion, and talk near $2 trillion is now seen as stale. One report said investors called $1.5 trillion a stretch.

Anthropic has not commented on these reports, and most of the figures come from secondary outlets rather than the company, so treat them as unconfirmed. The filing itself is the thing to watch: when the price range appears, it will show how much of the October growth story investors are willing to pay for.

What it means: the AI selloff arrived just as the largest AI listing of the year was getting ready to sell shares. A lower valuation would not change the business, but it would show how far the mood has moved since the filing went public.

articles.title: Bitcoin sits near $76,000 as ETF outflows continue
body: Bitcoin was trading around **$76,000** early Saturday, inside a narrow range after a failed attempt to recover above $80,000 this week. It fell 5.6% on Thursday, more than erasing an early gain on Wednesday, as traders dumped risk across tech and crypto after the stock rout. An IG analyst said it was dragged into the AI selloff.

US spot bitcoin ETFs lost about **$412 million** on Friday, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for roughly $403 million, and Ethereum ETFs lost about $93 million. It was the second straight heavy outflow day. The Block reported that cumulative net flows for bitcoin ETFs this year have turned slightly negative, down about $500 million since January.

Analyst Benjamin Cowen posted a video on Friday titled "Bitcoin: The Bears Strike Back." I could not confirm its contents, but his earlier framework held that buyers would need to defend a zone of roughly $73,000 to $77,000, and he has flagged a break below about $74,900 as a risk. Bitcoin is sitting on that line now.

What it means: bitcoin is trading with stocks again rather than as a hedge against them. If equities steady, the $75,000 area is the level to watch; if the Fed hike odds keep rising, ETF outflows could keep the pressure on.

articles.title: Starship Flight 15 now has a Nov. 13 target, but no license yet
body: SpaceX's vice president of launch, Kiko Dontchev, has named Friday, **Nov. 13** as the target for Starship Flight 15. Earlier FAA planning slides had shown Nov. 8 and then Nov. 12, so the date has slipped by about a day since the last update. The FAA's Starship page did not yet list a license for the flight, which still has to be issued before a launch.

The flight is expected to use Booster 22 and Ship 42. The plan is for the first time to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the ship with the launch tower's arms on the same flight. Gwynne Shotwell has said she expects the license to cover a return to the launch site and a tower catch for both stages.
One aggregator lists a placeholder date of Dec. 31, but that is not a real target. Until the FAA posts the license, treat Nov. 13 as a goal, not a schedule.

What it means: a double catch would be a major step toward reusing the ship, which SpaceX needs for its planned satellite and data-center work. A delay would not be surprising, and SpaceX's stock has been moving with the broader market this week.

vocab.def: Relating to twilight; describing animals that are most active at dawn and dusk.

cards.b: From Latin crepusculum, 'twilight'
dusky, dim, twilit
animals like rabbits, deer and owls that move around at dawn and dusk, or any soft low light

examples: The crepuscular glow made the whole street look gold.
Rabbits are crepuscular, so the best time to spot them is just after sunrise.
vocab.ex: The crepuscular glow made the whole street look gold.

cards.b: From Latin pellucidus, from per-, 'through', and lucidus, 'shining'
limpid, transparent, lucid
water or glass you can see through, and writing or explanations that are crystal clear

examples: The pond was so pellucid he could count the stones on the bottom.
Her pellucid explanation made the whole contract make sense.
vocab.ex: The pond was so pellucid he could count the stones on the bottom.

vocab.def: A soft whispering or rustling sound.

cards.b: From Latin susurrus, 'a whisper', a word that imitates its own sound
murmur, rustle, whisper
leaves, quiet voices, or water, anything that sounds like soft whispering

examples: A susurrus of leaves followed him down the trail.
The susurrus of the crowd settled as the lights went down.
vocab.ex: A susurrus of leaves followed him down the trail.

vocab.def: The earthy smell of rain falling on dry ground.

cards.b: Coined in 1964 by two Australian scientists from Greek petra, 'stone', and ichor, the fluid in the veins of the gods
the smell of rain, wet-earth scent
the fresh smell that rises when rain hits dry soil or pavement

examples: The petrichor after the first storm made the whole street smell alive.
She opened the window just to breathe in the petrichor.
vocab.ex: The petrichor after the first storm made the whole street smell alive.

vocab.def: Cheerful, quick readiness to do something.

cards.b: From Latin alacer, 'brisk, lively'
eagerness, readiness, promptness
answering a request quickly and willingly, with some enthusiasm

examples: She accepted the invitation with alacrity.
The new hires tackled the messy project with surprising alacrity.
vocab.ex: She accepted the invitation with alacrity.

vocab.def: Sweet and smooth to hear, like a voice or piece of music that flows easily.

cards.b: From Latin mel, 'honey', and fluere, 'to flow': literally 'flowing with honey'
dulcet, silken, honeyed
voices, music or prose that sounds smooth and pleasing

examples: The radio host's mellifluous voice made even the traffic report soothing.
She read the poem in a mellifluous whisper that quieted the room.
vocab.ex: The radio host's mellifluous voice made even the traffic report soothing.

vocab.def: Calm, peaceful and happy, often describing a time in the past that now seems golden.

cards.b: From Greek halkyon, a mythical kingfisher said to calm the winter seas while it nested
tranquil, idyllic, golden
a stretch of time you remember as untroubled, as in 'halcyon days'

examples: They talked about the halcyon summers they spent by the lake.
The long, quiet Sunday felt halcyon after a loud week.
vocab.ex: They talked about the halcyon summers they spent by the lake.

spanish.note: In Mexican Spanish, 'ya estuvo' closes something off. It can mean 'that's done', 'we're all set', or, with the right tone, 'that's enough'. Context and your voice do the work.

dialog.en: Do you still need anything from the store?
No, that's everything, thanks.
Sure? There's still time.
Yes, we're done. Let's go.

spanish.use: Say it when a task is finished, an order is complete, or you want to politely end something.

spanish.note: In Mexican Spanish, 'al rato' means 'in a while' or 'later', usually the same day. It's a loose way to say goodbye when you expect to see someone again soon.

dialog.en: I'm going to eat, shall we meet later?
Sure. What time do you finish?
Around four.
Perfect, see you in a bit.

spanish.use: Say it when you're parting ways and expect to meet again the same day.

spanish.meaning: Give me a shout / hit me up
spanish.note: In casual Mexican Spanish, 'echar un grito' means to get in touch, usually by call or message. People say it when making loose plans or ending a chat.

dialog.es: Voy a estar por tu zona el sábado.
dialog.en: I'll be in your area on Saturday.

dialog.es: ¡Qué bien! Échame un grito cuando llegues.
dialog.en: Great! Hit me up when you get here.
Okay, I'll hit you up.
Perfect, see you there.

spanish.use: Say it when you want a friend to get in touch about plans.

spanish.note: In Mexican Spanish, 'me late' means something sounds good or appeals to you, and it works for plans, ideas and offers. Its opposite is 'no me late', I'm not feeling it.

dialog.es: ¿Qué tal si cenamos en el mercado y luego caminamos?
dialog.en: How about dinner at the market and then a walk?

dialog.es: Me late la idea. ¿A qué hora?
dialog.en: I like that idea. What time?

dialog.es: Como a las siete, para agarrar mesa.
dialog.en: Around seven, so we can get a table.
Perfect, see you there.

spanish.use: Say it when a friend proposes a plan and you like it.

spanish.note: A very common Mexican way to say yes to a plan. Órale is an all-purpose exclamation (alright, wow, come on) and va means 'it's on'.

dialog.es: ¿Nos vemos a las siete para unos tacos?
dialog.en: Want to meet at seven for tacos?
Alright, let's do it!

dialog.es: Yo llego primero y pido mesa.
dialog.en: I'll get there first and get a table.
Perfect, see you there.

spanish.use: Say it when a friend proposes a plan and you are in.

spanish.meaning: Can you give me a hand?
spanish.note: Literally 'do you throw me the hand?'. Everyday Mexican for asking for help, from carrying boxes to fixing a problem.

cards.en: Give me a hand with this
Can I help you with something?

dialog.es: Voy a mover este sillón y está bien pesado.
dialog.en: I'm going to move this couch and it's really heavy.
Can you give me a hand?
Sure, where do I grab it?

dialog.es: Tú de ese lado, yo de este.
dialog.en: You on that side, me on this one.

spanish.use: Say it to a friend or coworker when you need help with something that takes two people.

options: Can you give me a hand?

spanish.meaning: Can you give me a ride?
spanish.note: 'Aventón' is the everyday Mexican word for a lift. You'll also hear 'raite', borrowed from English 'ride'.

dialog.es: Se me fue el camión y ya voy tarde.
dialog.en: I missed the bus and I'm already late.
I'm headed downtown.
Can you give me a ride?
Sure, hop in.

spanish.use: Say it to a friend or coworker who's driving where you're going.

options: Can you give me a ride?
Can you tell me the time?

phrases: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima
Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos

idea.body: In experiments, people who wrote gratitude notes underestimated how surprised and happy the recipient would be, and overestimated how awkward the note would feel. The hesitation is usually wrong.

dare.title: Go look for a burrowing owl
dare.why: Walk out to Shoreline Park by the Kite Lot this afternoon, an hour before sunset, and look for the little owls that spend the winter in the grass near their burrows. Walk slowly, stay on the trail, keep at least 50 feet back, and put your phone away so you actually see something. You may see nothing. Looking is the whole dare.

place.name: Shoreline Park, Kite Lot
place.sub: Mountain View, a short ride away

dare.worth: Burrowing owls are tiny, stand upright at the mouth of a hole, and are one of the few birds that live in plain sight of a tech campus. Spotting one makes the neighborhood feel like somewhere you've never quite looked at.

swap.title: Name one bird you can hear
swap.why: Step outside for five minutes, stand still, and listen. Pick the loudest bird, open a free bird-ID app, and match its call. Say its name out loud once.
swap.worth: Once a sound has a name, you start hearing it everywhere.
